title: Quant onboarding — weekly reflections (Jan 19, 2026)
body:
TL;DR: This week we continued onboarding two mid-sized open models (7B and 13B) to the compact quant profile. Early results: ~2.3–2.7x token-per-second gain on p3.8x compared to baseline FP16 when using grouped-4bit (g4) with KV cache preserved; perplexity on held-out evals up ~0.8–1.6% relative (task dependent). Main blockers are intermittent KV-cache corruption when mixing cold starts + g4-loaded checkpoints and a remaining accuracy regression on the summarization evals set.

Standup highlights (1/19):
- Marco: microbench sweep on 13B g4 + per-layer-remap reduced memory by ~38% vs FP16 and lowered tail latency 95th by ~18ms. Observed rare ~0.2% token-mismatch on sequential generation tests.
- Priya: set up evaluation harness to compare conversational instruction-following across quant formats (g4, g4+ptq, int8-reuse). Ran 250-shot pairwise A/B tests; prepping crowd-eval plan.
- Leah: Canary rollout plan drafted for Dedicated clusters; added automatic fallback to FP16 when model returns >3% token mismatch or rate of NLL spikes.
- Me (Evan): triaged KV-cache bug, reproduced locally with sequence-length >2048 and batch interleaving; suspect an index off-by-one in kv-merge for remapped tensors. Patch PR opened (GH: quant-probes#482).

Experiment log (concise):
- EXP-042 (13B, g4, baseline kernel v2): throughput 2.6x, p95 112ms (vs FP16 p95 130ms), eval-Rouge-L delta -1.3, perplexity +1.1. Notes: good perf, small quality hit on long-form summarization.
- EXP-047 (7B, g4+per-layer-ptq, kernel v2+prefetch): throughput 2.3x, p95 86ms (FP16 p95 105ms), eval-BLEU unchanged, but hallucination rate on entity tests up from 1.8% -> 2.9%.
- EXP-050 (13B, int8-reuse, fallback disabled): throughput 1.9x, p95 120ms, perplexity +0.8, stable KV across short sequences.

Known issues / open questions:
- KV-cache corruption when mixing warm and cold KV entries in remapped quant tensors. Repro steps documented in GH issue — likely merge logic when chunk boundaries align with remap offsets. Need pair debugging session with infra.
- Summarization regression: quality hit concentrated on multi-paragraph prompts where model must preserve citations/numbered items. Hypothesis: quant noise accumulates across long context windows due to high-sparsity in attention projections after remap. Short-term mitigation: increase per-layer calibration precision for cross-attention layers.
- Evaluation fidelity: our synthetic evals (perplexity/nll) undercount hallucination regressions seen in human evaluations. We need a small targeted crowd A/B for summarization and QA. Priya proposed a 200-prompt set with human labels; budget says ~$1.2k, approved by product.

Action items (owner | due):
- Evan: finish kv-merge patch and run full regression harness (including interleaved batches) | 2026-01-22
- Marco: run per-layer precision sweep focusing on cross-attention layers, push kernel toggles for v2.1 | 2026-01-25
- Priya: finalize 200-prompt crowd-eval spec and open microtask on platform; add annotation schema for hallucination + correctness | 2026-01-23
- Leah: implement canary policy that flips to FP16 at >2.5% mismatch or >5% increase in error-rate; add dashboard metric for token-mismatch-rate | 2026-01-26

Rollout / shipping notes:
- Proposed canary: Dedicated pool with 4 nodes, low traffic (10 rps), models pinned to quant-version: v0.9-g4. Canary metric set: p95 latency, token-mismatch-rate, NLL spike count. If threshold breached, auto-fallback to FP16.
- Backfill plan: Do not retroactively convert saved checkpoints; instead maintain dual artifacts: {modelname}-fp16 and {modelname}-g4. Keep mapping in model-catalog and mark recommended by workload.

Mini post-mortem (last week's failure):
- Incident: Canary on 01/14 triggered due to sudden token-mismatch spike; root cause traced to an optimizer that dumped remap indices with truncated dtype during checkpoint write. Fix: add explicit dtype-tag to checkpoint manifest and validation in loader. Deployed hotfix; tests added.

Notes to self / rough ideas:
- Try hybrid scheme: g4 for FF layers, per-layer int8 for attention QKV to reduce attention projection noise. Could be a sweet spot for summarization.
- Add automated long-context chain-of-thought probe tests that assert citation/ordering stability across quant variants.
- Explore training-aware PTQ (calibrate on generated chains rather than only token-level cross-entropy) — would probably reduce hallucination delta.

Links / quick refs (inlined):
- Repro for KV bug: GH issue link (quant-probes#482) — includes seed script and minimal docker image.
- Canary policy draft: confluence link in header.
- Eval harness: GH: redwood-inference/eval-harness, branch: quant-jan26

Meeting adjourned. Next sync: weekly standup Friday 2026-01-23 10:30 PT. Suggest splitting into two short topics: 1) KV merge deep-dive, 2) crowd-eval review.

Unresolved risks (short):
- If per-layer calibration increases memory footprint by >8% we lose part of throughput gains — need cost analysis before enabling by default.
- Operator experience: rollbacks must be fast and observable; add signal that shows token-level diffs for sampled requests in the console.

Raw scratch (things to possibly add later):
- Quick benchmark numbers vs gpt-3.5 baseline for marketing paper (tps and $/k tokens).
- Short script to sample 50 failing summarization cases and generate minimal debugging traces (KV contents + attention norm hist).
